# Initial implementation acceptance

Acceptance applies to exact tested combinations. Record SHA, OS, CLI versions, backend/socket, auth mode, command, result and missing evidence.

1. Launch actual installed Codex and Claude through managed tmux sessions. Identify work and execution independently of names, workspace, PID or pane ID. Unknown account/model identity remains explicit.
2. Link an exact existing session. Explain observed/bridge/managed capabilities immediately; no arbitrary PTY adoption or semantic delivery claims.
3. Select the correct real session in the TUI and enter its native terminal. Verify Unicode, alternate screen, resize, Ctrl-C, escape keys and detach. Return to the same work/group selection.
4. Stop/restart the TUI, then the daemon. The existing CLI survives where supported; reconcile exact runtime markers; do not launch a duplicate process. Test tmux loss separately and report missing execution.
5. Lose an acknowledgement around launch. Persist and reconcile operation identity rather than replaying a possibly completed start.
6. Race cooperating writable clients. Resolve one managed input owner, distinguish read-only attachment, and explain same-user direct tmux limitations.
7. With two real CLIs and ten sessions, find/open work quickly without mandatory grouping. Restore available place, drafts and selection; preserve unrelated local config.
8. Route two-server permitted inventory and a native terminal through one entry connection. Reconnect/revoke/partition tests must preserve authority and clearly distinguish gateway loss from task-home loss.
9. Exercise a supported model change and native resume/context handoff while retaining stable work/thread identity. Preserve queued input and do not repeat uncertain tool effects.
10. One shared authentication/resource problem yields one repair for its dependents. Existing native sign-in establishes actual identity; estimates and observed quota/cost remain distinct.
11. Supported bidirectional chat reaches the intended thread once; replay/echo/stale replies never submit unintended turns. Chat receipt is separate from provider acceptance.

Initial implementation may certify a subset and explicitly list the rest as planned/not run. Fixture processes and logical local hosts are useful automated evidence but never replace real CLI/native terminal/two-server acceptance.
